meta.title: Is my data safe? Tesuch security and data
meta.description: Where Tesuch keeps your data, who can see it, which services process it and how to start without risk. Only statements that can be checked.

hero.title: We designed Tesuch so that even if it were ever breached, there is almost nothing valuable to steal
hero.subtitle: Employees are stored as codes, not names. We keep only dates, never documents, salaries or passport data. Below is exactly what we keep, who processes it and what we do not claim.
hero.coverage: Tesuch checks, in part, {checked} of {total} items of the official labour inspection checklist. The rest are your documents.

facts.title: What we do to protect data

items.t: Data is stored in the EU
items.d: The database runs on Supabase in Ireland.

items.t: Each firm sees only its own data
items.d: Isolation is enforced inside the database (row-level security), not only in the app. Automated attack tests try to reach one firm’s data from another firm’s account, and they run in our test suite.

We store employee codes (names only if you turn them on), contract type and dates, probation end, leave records and the date of birth for the minors rule. We do not store documents, salaries, passport data, addresses or phone numbers.
The owner manages everything, including the team and the change history. The accountant edits data. The viewer can only read.

items.t: An audit log of every change
items.d: Every change to your data is recorded. Only owners can read the log, and nobody can edit it by hand.
Ask us and we export or delete your data.
All connections to Tesuch use HTTPS, so data is encrypted in transit.

processors.title: Who processes the data
processors.intro: Four services take part in processing. The same list is in the data processing agreement template.

items.name: Supabase
items.data: Everything you enter: accounts, companies, employees and contracts. Stored in Ireland.

items.name: Vercel
items.data: Serves the website and runs the application code. Requests from your browser pass through it.

items.name: Resend
items.data: The recipient’s email address and the text of the alert or weekly digest.

items.name: Telegram
items.data: Your Telegram chat ID and short summaries of issues, not full employee records.

processors.note: The question of transferring data across borders, including for Telegram, is still to be reviewed by a lawyer.
processors.dpa: Read the data processing agreement template

items.d: We do not claim ISO or SOC 2 certification, an independent audit or insurance.
The rules have not yet been reviewed by a lawyer, so every issue is marked “Advisory” until they are.
The data processing agreement template is a draft that still needs a lawyer’s review.

start.title: How to start without risk
start.intro: You can try everything before you enter any real data.

items.d: No account and no employee data are needed.
Sign in and load fictional companies to see how Tesuch works.
New businesses start with codes instead of names. Turn names on later, only if you want them.

items.t: Sign the agreement before real data
items.d: Before you load real data, sign the data processing agreement (DPA). A non-disclosure agreement (NDA) is available on request.

design.title: Built so there is little to steal
design.intro: Security starts with what we choose not to store. These are design choices, not promises about the future.

items.d: Employees are stored as codes such as EMP-014. Real names are optional and switched off for new businesses. You can turn them on later if you want them.
We keep what the rules need: contract type and dates, probation end, leave records, and the date of birth for the minors rule.
We do not store scanned documents, salaries, passport data, addresses or phone numbers. What is not stored cannot be stolen.

items.t: The free file check never uploads
items.d: When you try the free check with your staff file, it runs in your browser. The file does not leave your device.

design.honest: Honest line: no system can promise it will never be hacked. That is why we keep so little. If someone ever got in, they would find codes and dates, not a list of people with their documents and pay.
